memories.content: Use the same term throughout the proposal for the same interaction concept or interface element.
Use abbreviations only for recurring terms of three or more words.
Present the full name and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Prioritize the research role over diagnostic labels or deficits when referring to participants.
Reviewers from different subfields struggle to infer undefined abbreviations from context alone.
Use the term formative evaluation for studies seeking design modification evidence, and distinguish it from final efficacy judgments.
The user can have contribution labels such as principles, models, or guidelines approved only if they align with the abstraction level of the actual deliverables.
Design principles describe the relationship between conditions and outcomes rather than serving as instructions that merely replicate a single screen layout.
Link anticipated participant burden with its mitigation strategies for each field user study task.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the field system and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided in the field user study.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately upon collection.
List equipment to be loaned when participants lack necessary gear.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
The HCI ethics reviewer verifies that anticipated burden and mitigation strategies correspond for each field user study task.
Ensure that participants can safely return to existing work procedures if they discontinue research participation.
Specify that organizational members who decline research participation will not face disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.
The user's withdrawal risk can be adequately assessed only when a safe alternative procedure exists for field tasks.
The user tends to assume that a short session also entails little burden from work interruption and exposure to a manager.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate proposal concerns: the reference addresses terminology, participant framing, study characterization, and contribution labeling, while the compared frame addresses field-study ethics, accessibility, privacy, equipment, burden, withdrawal, and nonparticipation protections. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no terminology-consistency policy.
relations.summary: The reference alone requires consistent naming for the same interaction concept or interface element.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no rule governing when abbreviations are appropriate.
relations.summary: The reference alone limits abbreviations to recurring terms containing at least three words.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no first-use abbreviation rule.
relations.summary: The reference alone requires an abbreviation to accompany its full name at first use.

relations.reason: The compared frame addresses participant protections and access, not how participants should be named.
relations.summary: The reference alone prioritizes participants' research role over diagnostic or deficit-based labels.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no claim about reviewer comprehension of abbreviations.
relations.summary: The reference alone identifies cross-subfield reviewers' difficulty inferring undefined abbreviations.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no study-characterization terminology.
relations.summary: The reference alone reserves formative evaluation for design-modification evidence and distinguishes it from final efficacy judgments.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no contribution-labeling policy.
relations.summary: The reference alone conditions approval of contribution labels on alignment with the deliverables' abstraction level.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no definition of design principles.
relations.summary: The reference alone defines design principles as condition–outcome relationships rather than single-layout replication instructions.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no field-study burden-and-mitigation policy.
relations.summary: The compared frame alone requires task-level correspondence between anticipated participant burden and mitigation strategies, including reviewer verification.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no accessibility-accommodation requirement.
relations.summary: The compared frame alone requires identification of accommodations needed for access to the field system and research tasks.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no accommodation-delivery requirement.
relations.summary: The compared frame alone requires an account of how accessibility accommodations will be provided.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no research-data privacy procedure.
relations.summary: The compared frame alone requires immediate separation of personal identifiers from research data at collection.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no equipment-access provision.
relations.summary: The compared frame alone requires listing equipment that will be loaned to participants lacking necessary gear.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no equipment-return procedure.
relations.summary: The compared frame alone requires a return procedure for equipment loaned to participants.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no withdrawal or field-task fallback policy.
relations.summary: The compared frame alone requires a safe alternative work procedure for discontinued participation and treats that alternative as necessary for assessing withdrawal risk.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no organizational nonparticipation protection.
relations.summary: The compared frame alone protects organizational members who decline participation from disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no claim about hidden sources of field-study burden.
relations.summary: The compared frame alone identifies a tendency to underestimate work-interruption and managerial-exposure burdens when sessions are short.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only guidance covers burden mitigation, accommodations, identifier separation, equipment loans, safe withdrawal, protection from nonparticipation penalties, and risks from work interruption or managerial exposure.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only guidance covers consistent terminology, abbreviation discipline, participant-centered language, formative evaluation, and contribution labels grounded in deliverable abstraction.
